- Ensure compatibility with Java 17+ as per Spring Framework 6.0.

- The porting involves adapting modules to work with Spring Cloud Data Stream's API and dependencies.

- The shell commands will use REST API calls to the Spring Cloud Data server.

- Unit tests and integration tests will be written for all new code.

- The development environment is set up with necessary tools and libraries.

- No major changes to the existing codebase; primarily porting and adapting.

- Effort estimates are for a single developer working on this task.

Activity 6: Port tcp module. Similar to http, but for tcp. Estimate: 20 hours.

Activity 7: Port twitterstream module. Estimate: 24 hours (assuming it might be more complex due to Twitter API).

Activity 8: Port twittersearch module. Similar to twitterstream. Estimate: 24 hours.

Activity 9: Port filter module. For processor module. Estimate: 16 hours.

Activity 10: Port transform module. For processor module. Estimate: 16 hours.

So, total most likely effort: 208 work-hours.

Develop a strategy using Spring's ConfigurationProperties to expose module metadata for properties and configuration.
Code the shell command to display module properties and metadata based on the derived strategy.
Adapt the http source module from Spring XD to work with Spring Cloud Data Stream, ensuring it functions as a source module.
Adapt the tcp source module from Spring XD to work with Spring Cloud Data Stream, ensuring it functions as a source module.

Move the twittersearch source module from Spring XD to Spring Cloud Data Stream, adapting it for current Twitter API and integration.
Adapt the filter processor module from Spring XD to work with Spring Cloud Data Stream, ensuring it functions as a processor module.
Adapt the transform processor module from Spring XD to work with Spring Cloud Data Stream, ensuring it functions as a processor module.
Perform integration testing of the entire software increment, identify and fix any bugs or issues that arise.
Write documentation for the new shell commands and ported modules, and conduct a code review to ensure code quality and standards.
